mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 4% in the month preceding the decision is associated with a near-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to reduced risk-free discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4.0% in the prior month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the month following the rate hike (t-test p > 0.05), or the S&P 500 5-day return immediately after the hike is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in UNRATE exceeding 0.2 percentage points coincides with a positive 20-day S&P 500 forward return as lower labor-market expectations reduce equity risk premia.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE rises by more than 0.2pp in the current month
failure_condition: Over 10 consecutive months of UNRATE increases ≤ 0.2pp, or 20-day forward returns are negative despite UNRATE increases > 0.2pp.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly index of industrial production (INDPRO) exceeds 102.0 while the prior month is below 101.5, it signals a strengthening supply-side momentum that is associated with a positive 60-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO crosses above 101.5 while previous month < 101.5
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not statistically positive (t-test p > 0.05) during such INDPRO breakouts over 5 consecutive quarters.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous monthly declines in both HOUST (housing starts) and PAYEMS (employment) indicate a dual softening in demand indicators, predicting a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: both HOUST and PAYEMS fall in the same month
regime_hint: Dual softening in housing and labor markets
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.05) when both proxies decline, or the interaction coefficient in a two-variable regression is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in GDPC1 (real GDP) below trend is followed by a negative 60-day S&P 500 forward return as investor uncertainty rises and risk aversion increases.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain positive despite 3 consecutive quarters of GDPC1 below trend (measured via rolling mean), or the correlation with SPX 60d returns is not statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: When the CPIAUCSL inflation index exceeds 215.0 for two consecutive months, the S&P 500 is expected to deliver a negative 20-day forward return as market anticipates rate hikes that erode equity value.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 215.0 and remains above for at least 2 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative during or immediately after the inflation breakout (p > 0.05), or the S&P 500 5-day return after the first breakout month is positive.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly RSAFS (retail sales) above 350 billion dollars, accompanied by a decline in UNRATE below 7%, signals a shift toward consumer optimism and reduced wage pressure, predicting a positive 5-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS > 350 and UNRATE < 7.0 in the same month
regime_hint: Optimism rebound in consumer spending amid labor moderation
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not positive when the interaction is statistically insignificant (p > 0.05) or RSAFS rises while UNRATE does not fall.

mechanism_narrative: During a regime of falling industrial production (INDPRO < 100) for three consecutive months, the S&P 500 60-day forward return is expected to be negative due to persistent supply-side weakness and reduced corporate earnings growth.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not negative during any 3-month INDPRO contraction period (rolling mean), or the average 60-day return during contractions exceeds zero.
